editorial:
Imagine you have almost no money, a beat up car, and the only friend you have in the world is your dog. That is exactly where you start with this story. You follow Wendy, a woman trying to get to Alaska for a job, but she gets stuck in a small town. The movie feels very real and quiet, almost like you are just hanging out with her as she tries to survive. It is not a loud movie with big explosions, but it captures that feeling of being totally alone and scared that everything is falling apart around you.

The acting is amazing because it feels so natural, like the actors aren't even acting. You will feel for Wendy as she searches for her dog, even if the slow pace makes you a bit restless at times. If you like stories about the struggle to get by, you will love this. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, or if you really love the art of film, adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move. It is a slow burn, but it hits hard by the end.
endingExplained: After searching everywhere, Wendy realizes she cannot find her dog and she has run out of money and options. In the final scenes, she has to make the heartbreaking choice to leave Lucy at a shelter. She walks away alone, knowing she cannot take care of the dog anymore. It is a sad ending because there is no magic fix, but it shows how hard life can be when you have nothing left.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quiet character studies and emotional stories about friendship.
